
=================================================================
#34 Stallion Mountain  (645 June)
Arc: Part II — The Dawn of War / The Seventh Invasion · place: jupil · tone: epic war — clash of heroes
Logline: A farmer in a white coat walks onto the field as a name on a muster roll. The Emperor is watching.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Go Yeonsu liked the old man’s story. He just didn’t think it was about him.
[1] [PLACE jupil: Named for where an emperor stopped. Emperors name a lot of things.]
[2] [MAP 645: Goguryeo sends a hundred and fifty thousand down the crow road. The emperor sends himself.]
[3] ¶ At Stallion Mountain the Second Emperor does not wait behind the line.
[4] The Second Emperor: I myself am the **vanguard**…!
[5] ¶ The relief army comes down the crow road under banners that think numbers are an argument. **Go Yeonsu** and **Go Hyejin** ride at the front. Across the plain, under a hill, the Tang look like a single army of fifteen thousand.
[6] The old officer: That isn’t all of them. / An emperor doesn’t come this far with fifteen thousand. Dig in. Cut his grain. Let winter do the fighting.
[7] Go Yeonsu: Winter isn’t here, grandfather. He is. In person. / We will never get a better chance at an emperor’s head.
[8] ¶ Nobody tells Go Yeonsu about the valley behind him. A second army has gone round through it in the night, with the Black Dragon at its head.
[9] ¶ At dawn, drums start on the mountain above the field. The emperor is up there with his horns and his flags, playing the battle like a court orchestra.
[10] ── SCENE: The Tang Line ──
[11] ¶ In the Tang line stands a guard captain whose accent still has the sea in it. Sul Gedu left Silla twenty-four winters ago, in the hold of a merchant ship. When the emperor called for volunteers, he put his own name down. It’s the only way a foreigner gets a captain’s sash. Across the field, the enemy’s banners are close enough to read.
[12] 🪖: Hey, Captain Xue. That lot over there… they say they’re Samhan men. / Aren’t you from Samhan as well?
[13] Sul Gedu: Samhan. Silla. / In Silla they count your bones before they hire you. Doesn’t matter how big your talent is or how big your deeds — wrong bones, and you don’t get over the wall. You just don’t. / So I crossed the sea. To walk in and out at the Son of Heaven’s side with a cap and a sash and a sword. / …That’ll do me.
[14] ¶ The soldier laughs, not sure he was meant to. Sul Gedu ties off his helmet cord and does not look at the banners again.
[15] ¶ In the Tang line a low officer decides the field needs a mark it cannot look away from. He puts on **white armour** — not for mourning, for visibility — hangs two bows at his waist, takes up the **fangtian ji**, and rides into the front so hard the relief army has to notice him or die without knowing why.
[16] Xue Rengui: Make a path. / If you will not — the ji will.
[17] ¶ No one in the Goguryeo line stops him for long. Then the drums on the mountain change, and the Black Dragon’s banners come out of the valley behind them. The relief army turns to face the wrong way twice. The formation breaks. The mountain learns a new colour.
[18] ❝QUOTE (Zizhi Tongjian (資治通鑑) bk. 198, Tang Zhenguan 19 (645), 6th month): Just then came thunder and lightning. Xue Rengui, a man of Longmen, in strange clothing, broke into the enemy line with a great shout, and nothing could stand before him. The Goguryeo troops gave way; the main army followed through, and the Goguryeo troops broke completely…❞
[19] The Second Emperor: Who is that man in white armour. / The one at the tip of the spear.
[20] Blue Dragon: Xue Rengui, Your Majesty. / A soldier… who was a farmer.
[21] ¶ They bring him up. Dirt on the white. Blood on the crescent of the ji. He kneels like a man who has never been in a palace and does not intend to apologise for it.
[22] The Second Emperor: My old generals are all aged. / I have been looking for a fierce one to entrust the frontier to — and I find none better than you. / I am less happy about gaining Liaodong than about gaining you.
[23] Xue Rengui: A farmer… how could he dare. / This ji only widened Your Majesty’s road a little.
[24] ¶ They give him gold, silk, a general’s title, and a place among the men who stand at the northern gate. The white coat stays. So does the ji.
[25] ¶ That night he has a clerk write home for him. Two lines. The mounds can be finished properly now. Liu should buy the good stone.
[26] ¶ Go Yeonsu pulls what is left onto a hill to regroup. Behind the hill, the Tang have already burned the bridges. Nobody goes home the way they came. The emperor likes that trick.
[27] ¶ When the dust settles, the two relief commanders walk into the Tang camp and surrender. Thirty-six thousand men walk in behind them. The officers are sent inland, to be subjects far from any border. The common soldiers are sent home. The three thousand Mohe riders who came south with them are marched into a valley and buried alive.
[28] ¶ Go Yeonsu does not live out the year. The records say he died of grief, which is the only cause of death the Tang ever let a surrendered general keep.
[29] ── SCENE: The Field at Night ──
[30] ¶ There is another foreigner in the reckoning that night. Riding over the ground where the Goguryeo centre stood, the emperor finds Sul Gedu farther in than any of his own men got, face down among the dead he made.
[31] The Second Emperor: Who is this? / He is further in than any of Ours.
[32] Blue Dragon: A Silla man, Majesty. Sul Gedu. / His friends say he wanted a cap, a sash and a sword. At your side.
[33] The Second Emperor: Our own men look about them and will not advance. A foreigner dies for Us. / Give him the rank. Bury him with full rites.
[34] ¶ Then he takes off the imperial robe and lays it over the dead man himself.
[35] ¶ The cap, the sash and the sword, more or less. He gets them lying down.
[36] ¶ Fame is a short leash. Before the army even settles into the Ansi siege, Goguryeo stops trying to kill the man in white in the open and starts trying to keep him.
[37] ── SCENE: The Cell Under the Wall ──
[38] ¶ They take him in a night fight east of the Liao — nets, numbers, the ji knocked from his hands — and drag him inland to a lesser fortress that is not Ansi and does not want to be famous. Iron on the wrists. A cell under the wall. The white coat cut off him like a trophy.
[39] Gate Guard: The Second Emperor… is coming this way. / Tonight. With silver, to buy back the man in white. Holy King, look down.
[40] Xue Rengui: …Before His Majesty arrives. / I will have to be out.
[41] ¶ He breaks the irons. He breaks the door. The white coat only made him easy to see.
[42] ¶ He finds the ji on a rack in the yard, still sticky from someone else’s hands, and takes the wall the way water takes a crack. By the time the Second Emperor’s banners show on the ridge, the cell is empty and the fortress is explaining itself to no one.
[43] The Second Emperor: …That white coat again. / Arriving before Us, I see.
[44] Xue Rengui: I could not keep Your Majesty waiting. / The chains… were impolite.
[45] ¶ The Second Emperor laughs once — short, relieved — and does not ask how. A sovereign who has to ask how has already lost the man.
[46] ── SCENE: Two Boys ──
[47] ¶ Among the prisoners taken at the mountain are two boys, eleven and eight: Gesomun’s sons, the careful one and the one who never backs down first. Their father sent them with the baggage to watch an emperor run.
[48] The Second Emperor: So. Gai Suwen’s sons. / Your father killed his king. I killed my brothers. / So you see, he and I understand one another.
[49] The Second Emperor: Here is my offer. / Kneel, call yourselves servants of the Great Tang, and I will give you both titles. / A house in Chang’an, silk, a name. Things Goryeo will never give you.
[50] Yeon Namgun: Brother.
[51] ¶ Namseng is eleven. He works out, quite quickly, that the Second Emperor wants two and will settle for one, and that only one of them has to be the one who refuses.
[52] Yeon Namseng: Your Majesty. My brother is small. He understands nothing. / It is I who refuse. Give the punishment to me.
[53] The Second Emperor: …You are the elder?
[54] Yeon Namseng: I am.
[55] ¶ They flog him in front of his brother and send them both back across the Liao in the spring, as a gesture. Namgun does not speak for the whole journey.
[56] Yeon Namgun: You took it for me.
[57] Yeon Namseng: I am the elder.
[58] ── SCENE: Pyongyang ──
[59] ¶ The news reaches Pyongyang in two pieces. The field army is gone. The boys are in the emperor’s tent.
[60] Yeon Gesomun: Both of them?
[61] Rider: Both, Supreme Commander. The emperor sends word he will be kind to them.
[62] Yeon Gesomun: Kind. / A man who killed his brothers is being kind to my sons.
[63] ¶ The hall waits for him to break something. He doesn’t. He calls for a map and puts his thumb on the one fort still flying the old king’s colours. The fort that refused him.
[64] Yeon Gesomun: Ansi. That madman. / When I was seven, my father came home from the Colossal River with a Sui flag under his arm. I thought flags grew on emperors. / Let him come deep. The last one did.
[65] ¶ **Why isn’t Gesomun afraid? Go back thirty-three years, to a general who surrendered seven times and won…!**
